value.rationale: The natural first nontrivial periodicity question of the exact predator–prey recurrence receives a complete all-parameter answer, including the post-Neimark–Sacker regime that escapes the original source's parameter-restricted convergence theorem. Positive predator–prey two-season oscillations cannot occur even as isolated nonlocal cycles, an obstruction not implied by equilibrium multipliers. This distinguishes model-specific dynamics from Euler predator–prey maps that can undergo flip bifurcations and removes period two from future positive-cycle classifications.
